title: Lord Beaverbrook's party and the future King at the piano
summary: The band plays Beaverbrook's party; the Prince of Wales grabs Duke at the piano.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But let me tell you a little incident. This will kill you. So while I was in London in 1933, so Lord Beaverbrook, he's a Canadian, but he owns all the newspapers. You may have heard of him. He's big, big there. He would throw him a party so he throws this party at his mansion, you know, and
he had the guy that's married to the Queen now. He was just another turkey then, he wasn't married to her then. He hit the jackpot there.

So we don't have to carry no -- the guys carried their horns and didn't have to carry no bass and I didn't have to carry no drums. We play this party, Jack Hilton played till we got there. So we go in this party, we come in this party -- this is God's honest truth, this is not no illusion. This is the real thing. We come in this party and the place is crowded. At that time Jeannette McDonald, she was a big star, you know, she sang --

She was there as a guest. Anna Mae Wong, remember her, some movie star and a gang of American movie stars, so we pop in there. I will never forget it. We were all dressed in white because it was in the summer, you know, in July, we had on white uniforms and special made, white special made shoes, all sharp, so this guy that's married to the Queen now, he grabbed Duke right away and sit him down at the piano stool and they start playing -- see, he play piano and start playing and Duke, wait a minute -- he say, 'I got 500 of your records.'
He padlocked Duke right away. I go over to the drums and a little cat's sitting down on the floor and so then we played, played and played and before we started playing there
